📅 What this is
The state sets the tasks and how many days a week each one is approved for. The consumer only chooses which days. They do that on the form above, at orientation, and it arrives here signed.

WellSky has no open API, so nobody can push these days into it for you. What this page does instead is lay them out as a week grid you can read straight down while you build the schedule, and keep a signed copy for the consumer's file. Tick Built in WellSky when it is in, and it leaves the queue.

⛔ What will fail the audit
A W-9 is not proof. It is self-reported, not issued by the IRS. This is the most common way to fail while believing you complied.
A number typed into a letter or spreadsheet is not proof. It has to come from the IRS or the Missouri Department of Revenue with the legal name and number already on it.
The wrong category is not an upload. If it is not filed under EIN Tax Documents, treat it as missing.
Entered but not uploaded, or uploaded but not entered, is still a finding. Both halves are required.
Two free passes: a single document showing both numbers covers both, and no upload is needed at all where a previous CDS vendor already uploaded proof to that case record.

Onboarding Checklists
🎓 Orientation Completions

Every finished online orientation posts itself here the moment the learner completes it — name, date, score, and whether all seven acknowledgments were checked. This is the case-file proof of training per 19 CSR 15-8.400(5)(H)5: print the learner’s completion page for the file, and use this list to see who has finished without waiting for paper. Courses live at caringcds.com/consumer-orientation/ and /attendant-orientation/.

Loading…
🧭 CDS Attendant Onboarding, step by step

The attendant works for the consumer. Our job is to make sure they are allowed to work in CDS and get paid. Goal: about 20 office minutes per attendant. Each attendant's profile (Attendants, then tap their name) shows their next step with "How do I do this?".

1
Application (attendant, on their own)
The consumer sends their caregiver to caringcds.com/apply. You get an alert the moment Step 1 is signed. A consumer waiting means it is due today.
2
Checks (office, about 10 minutes)
OIG runs by itself. Run FCSR and EDL from their profile with the Copy buttons, on every name and every SSN they listed. Record each result with its screenshot. Nobody works before all checks are clear.
!
If the FCSR finds something
Check it against the FCSR "cannot hire" list (MMAC), then tap Something came up on their profile and pick one:
  • On the list: they need a Good Cause Waiver. The hub texts and emails them the steps. No shifts and no Step 2 papers while it is pending. Every 2 weeks you get a to-do to check the waiver status on the FCSR site (Good Cause Waiver tab, Waiver Status). When the approval letter comes, add it and pick Clear to continue or Not moving forward.
  • On the EDL: they cannot work in CDS. A waiver is not possible.
  • Not on the list (for example a misdemeanor): clear after review, nothing is sent.
Either way you get a to-do to call the consumer. You tell the consumer, not the hub. Not sure? Call MMAC at 573-751-3399.
3
Orientation video and handbook (attendant)
The links are on their last Step 1 screen and sent by text and email. Reminders go out by themselves.
4
Papers (attendant)
Opens when checks are clear: Attendant Care Contract, pay rate, unit agreement, handbook.
5
Empeon (office, about 3 minutes)
Copy for Empeon, send the invite, tap Empeon invite sent. W-4, I-9, direct deposit and ID photos happen in Empeon.
6
ID call (office, 5 minutes)
Video call: they hold up the same ID they uploaded. Tap ID seen, finish I-9 Section 2 in Empeon (remote box), countersign the contract.
7
First shift
They clock in with the WellSky app or the consumer's home phone. The hub sees the first shift from the WellSky email and moves them to Working.
Links: FCSR provider login · FCSR "cannot hire" list · Good Cause Waiver: how to apply · MMAC: FCSR for CDS providers · EDL · OIG search · Section 192.2495 RSMo
Rechecks after they start: OIG every month (runs by itself), EDL every 3 months, FCSR every year. Keep FCSR and waiver papers 5 years.
👤 New Consumer Onboarding Checklist

All documents are collected via GoHighLevel e-sign and the orientation is self-serve, so no in-person meeting is required. The annual home visit is the only in-person contact. There is still an onboarding specialist call before the first shift, at step 11b.

STEP 1 — ELIGIBILITY & AUTHORIZATION
1
Receive & Date-Stamp Authorization — Clock Starts Now
Stamp the date received on the authorization immediately upon receipt. Services must begin within 7 calendar days (or the authorization start date, whichever is later). If you cannot start in time, place written justification in the consumer's file and send a copy to the DHSS case manager. Confirm consumer is MO HealthNet eligible, 18+, able to self-direct care.
Reg: 19 CSR 15-8.400 §5; P&P Policy 5
2
Review DHSS-Approved Plan of Care
Obtain the approved plan of care from DHSS/DSDS. Note the authorized hours, units, and specific tasks. Services must be delivered strictly per the care plan — do not provide any task not authorized.
Reg: CDS Program Req. §2.2
3
Verify TPL Insurance & Medicare Before Proceeding
Ask the consumer about other insurance coverage before billing MO HealthNet. If they have private insurance or Medicare, that must be billed first — MO HealthNet is payer of last resort. Verify via IVR: (573) 635-8908 or emomed.com. Document TPL status in consumer file.
Reg: P&P Policy 9; CDS Program Req. §3.3(c)
STEP 2 — CONSUMER ENROLLMENT PACKET (GoHighLevel)
4
Send Consumer to caringcds.com/onboarding — Two-Step GoHighLevel Flow
Direct the consumer to caringcds.com/onboarding. This is a connected two-step GoHighLevel flow — their basic info prefills all documents automatically:
  • Step 1 (caringcds.com/onboarding) — Consumer fills out basic info survey; info prefills all enrollment documents
  • Step 2 (caringcds.com/onboarding-packet) — Consumer reviews and e-signs all prefilled enrollment documents, including: Consumer Vendor Acknowledgement, Authorization to Obtain Employment Numbers, Previous CDS Vendor Authorization (PCCP transfers), Telephony/EVV Consent Form, Consumer Emergency Back-Up Plan, Form 8821, Form SS-4, Form 2678, Form 2643A, Form 2827
⚠️ Do NOT send the Training Acknowledgement Form in this packet — consumer must complete orientation first (Step 3 below).
Reg: CDS Program Req. §2.3(e); P&P Policy 3
STEP 3 — CONSUMER ORIENTATION (Before Training Ack)
5
Direct Consumer to Complete Online Orientation
Send consumer to caringcds.com/orientation to:
  • Watch the CDS orientation videos
  • Review the CDS Handbook
The orientation covers all required training topics: consumer eligibility, plan of care, consumer responsibilities and rights, what consumers are not allowed to do, emergency backup plan, maintaining eligibility, denial/termination/reduction, grievance procedures, disaster policy, how to recruit/hire/train/supervise attendants, vendor responsibilities, required background checks, attendant qualifications and responsibilities, mandated reporting, fraud prevention, HIPAA, EVV, allowable/non-allowable tasks, and essential transportation.
Reg: 19 CSR 15-8.400; MMAC Vendor Responsibilities; P&P Policy 7
6
Send Training Acknowledgement Form via GoHighLevel (After Orientation)
After consumer has watched the videos and reviewed the handbook, send the Consumer Training Acknowledgement Form via GoHighLevel for e-signature. This form documents that the consumer has been trained on all required CDS program topics. Acknowledgement form must be placed in consumer file. If consumer needs help, offer to walk them through orientation by phone.
Reg: CDS Program Req. §5.18; P&P Policy 7
6b
Collect Their Scheduling Preferences
The state's plan of care fixes the tasks and how many days a week each one is approved for. The consumer chooses which days. Take those choices on hub.caringcds.com/care-plan/, which holds them to the approved number of days and will not let them pick a fourth day on a three-day task.

It arrives signed under Consumers → Care Plan Days laid out as a week grid to build the WellSky schedule from. Tick Built in WellSky once it is in. WellSky has no open API, so nothing can push it there for you.
Replaces the old GoHighLevel scheduling preferences document, whose signed output was an image nobody could read
STEP 4 — PROCESS TAX FORMS (After Signed Packet Received)
7
Submit SS-4 — Obtain Federal EIN for Consumer
Using the signed SS-4 and Authorization to Obtain Employment Numbers, obtain the consumer's Federal EIN online via irs.gov. Consumer is registered as a "Household Employer (HCSR)." Record EIN in consumer file.
8
Submit Form 8821 & Form 2678 to IRS
File Form 8821 (Tax Information Authorization) and Form 2678 (Appointment of Agent) with the IRS. These authorize Caring Companions to handle federal payroll tax reporting and payments on the consumer's behalf. Form 2678 covers Forms 940 and 941.
9
Submit Form 2643A & Form 2827 to Missouri
Submit MO Form 2643A (Tax Registration — "New Consumer-Directed Services Participant") to MO Department of Revenue. Submit Form 2827 (MO Power of Attorney — Withholding) to authorize Caring Companions for state tax matters. Mail to: Taxation Division, P.O. Box 357, Jefferson City MO 65105-0357. Note consumer's MO Tax ID when received.
MO Revenue: (573) 751-5860 | businesstaxregister@dor.mo.gov
10
Register Consumer in UInteract (DES) — Missouri UI Tax Only
⚠️ Timing: UInteract registration can ONLY happen AFTER first payroll is issued AND consumer has paid at least $1,000 in wages in a single quarter. Do not attempt before then — DES will not issue an account number.

NEW Consumer (never had a CDS vendor before):
Login to uinteract.labor.mo.gov → Employer Registration → Register Employer. Enter consumer's EIN and SSN. Type of Organization = "Individual Ownership." Business type = "Health Care / Social Assistance / Services for Elderly and Persons with Disabilities." Domestic employment = Yes. Enter consumer's home address as headquarters. Enter wage history (gross wages per quarter). Submit. The confirmation screen shows the consumer's MO Unemployment Tax Account Number (EAN) and is the only place it appears during registration, so record it before closing the window. If you lose it: Inquiry → Tax Inquiry → Client List Details lists every consumer with their EAN. The full screen-by-screen walkthrough is in the consumer's Tax Setup window under step 5.

TRANSFERRED Consumer (came from another CDS vendor):
If you are not sure whether they were with another vendor, try registering them in UInteract first. If it errors, they are a transfer. Then email MODES-5083 (Transferred Consumer Registration form) to cdstax@labor.mo.gov after their first payroll with you. Need: consumer's EIN, SSN, first payroll date with you, name of previous vendor. Download form: labor.mo.gov/media/22536/download

After registration: File quarterly wage reports per consumer (Q1 Apr 30 / Q2 Jul 31 / Q3 Oct 31 / Q4 Jan 31). Wages reported under consumer's account — NEVER under Caring Companions' account. Separate payment per consumer — do NOT combine.

Parent attendant exception: If attendant is a parent of the consumer, wages are NEVER reportable for UI purposes — do not report them.
General questions: cdstax@labor.mo.gov | 573-751-1995 Opt. 1 | Delinquent/penalties: Christopher Matzke 573-751-1867 | Wage reporting/adjustments: Kristie Riedmann 573-751-1995 x4105
10b
Local Tax Registration — Kansas City or St. Louis Consumers Only
If the consumer lives within Kansas City or St. Louis city limits, register for local payroll taxes. Not required for other Missouri locations.
STEP 5 — SETUP & GO-LIVE
11
Set Up Consumer in WellSky Personal Care (EVV & Billing)
Enroll consumer in WellSky Personal Care — our EVV AND billing platform. Confirm attendant and consumer both understand EVV clock-in/clock-out procedure and the Saturday 11:59 PM weekly correction deadline. All MO HealthNet billing flows through WellSky. Portal: mycaringcds.com
11b
Onboarding Specialist Call — Before the First Shift
The orientation is self-serve, but somebody rings them before the first shift. It is not a courtesy call: it is where the things that stop them being paid get caught.

Cover three things:
1. Can the attendant actually clock in? Either the WellSky Personal Care app on their own phone, or telephony from the consumer's home phone if that suits them better. Have them do it while you are on the line rather than taking their word for it. Getting this wrong means unpaid hours, not a warning.
2. What to do when a shift needs correcting. Walk them through the EVV Correction Form, which is how they ask us to change a shift, and the Saturday 11:59 PM deadline each week. Nobody reads that page for the first time calmly, so show them before they need it.
3. Anything left over from the orientation. They have just read the handbook and watched the videos on their own, so ask what did not make sense.
Also the moment to confirm the scheduling preferences from step 6b match what they expect
12
Establish Consumer Case File
Create complete consumer file with all of the following:
  • Date-stamped authorization + Plan of Care
  • All signed GoHighLevel e-sign documents (Vendor Ack, Auth to Obtain Numbers, Previous Vendor Auth, EVV Consent, Training Ack)
  • Signed Emergency Back-Up Plan (names + phone numbers of backup caregiver)
  • TPL/insurance documentation
  • All tax form copies (SS-4, 8821, 2678, 2643A, 2827)
  • EVV and WellSky enrollment confirmation
Reg: CDS Program Req. §5.23; P&P Policy 6
13
Schedule First Monthly Case Management Contact
Begin monthly monitoring cadence — phone or in-person. Document all contacts in consumer file. The required annual face-to-face home visit counts as a contact; schedule it within the first year.
Reg: 19 CSR 15-8.400(4)(F)
🧑‍🤝‍🧑 New Attendant Onboarding Checklist

Two platforms, in this order: the application is a GoHighLevel document, and Empeon is for the hiring paperwork once the checks come back clear. No in-person meeting required. Complete ALL steps before the attendant begins providing services, no exceptions.

STEP 1 — INTAKE (Attendant Self-Serve)
1
Send the Attendant Application — GoHighLevel, Not Empeon Yet
Send the attendant application as a GoHighLevel document for e-signature. This comes before Empeon: the application is what lets us run the checks, and there is no point setting somebody up for payroll who has not cleared them.

The application must capture: (a) disclosure of ALL criminal convictions and pleas; (b) authorisation to obtain criminal background information; (c) consent to release closed records (§610.120 RSMo); (d) ALL aliases and SSNs ever used; (e) whether they have lived outside Missouri in the last five years.

Do not run any background check until the signed application is back, because the consent to look is on it.
Platform: GoHighLevel documents | Reg: CDS Program Req. §4.2.1
STEP 2 — PRE-HIRE SCREENING (After Signed Packet Received)
2
FCSR — Family Care Safety Registry Check
Screen ALL aliases and ALL SSNs disclosed. Check for: criminal history, sex offender registry, child abuse records, DHSS EDL, DMH EDR, child care license revocations. Retain documentation on file. If finding — verify whether disqualifying under RSMo 192.2495.
Reg: CDS Program Req. §4.1; 19 CSR 30-82.060
3
EDL — Employee Disqualification List Check
Check Missouri EDL at health.mo.gov/safety/edl — screen ALL known aliases. Do NOT hire anyone listed. Retain documentation.
Reg: RSMo 192.2490; CDS Program Req. §4.1
4
LEIE — OIG Exclusion List Check
Screen at exclusions.oig.hhs.gov. Screen ALL known aliases. Retain proof. Any exclusion discovered must be reported to MMAC immediately.
Reg: CDS Program Req. §5.2
5
Out-of-State Check — Has Attendant Lived Outside Missouri in Last 5 Years?
If YES: FCSR data is Missouri-only — you must also obtain background checks (criminal history, sex offender, child abuse/neglect registry) from each state the attendant lived in during the past 5 years. Additionally, a fingerprint-based background check is required for a national FBI criminal history search via Missouri State Highway Patrol (MSHP). Submit FBI FD-258 fingerprint card to MSHP CJIS Division, PO Box 9500, Jefferson City, MO 65102-9500 (4–6 week processing), or use IDEMIA (MO's fingerprint vendor) at (844) 543-9712. Out-of-state applicants can be fingerprinted by local law enforcement in their state. If NO (MO resident 5+ years): Standard FCSR check is sufficient for state criminal history.
MSHP CJIS Division: 573-526-6153 | IDEMIA: 844-543-9712 | FCSR: Missouri data only
6
Verify Attendant is NOT Consumer's Spouse
Attendant can be a family member (parent, sibling, child, grandparent) but CANNOT be the consumer's spouse or legal guardian. Obtain verification if needed.
Reg: §208.909; CDS Program Req. §4.4.1
7
E-Verify — Work Authorization
If agency qualifies as a "business entity" under RSMo 285.525, must enroll and participate in E-Verify. Run E-Verify on all new hires.
Reg: CDS Program Req. §4.5; RSMo 285.530
STEP 3 — HIRE DOCUMENTATION (After All Checks Clear)
8
Checks Cleared — Now Invite Them Into Empeon
Only once FCSR, EDL and OIG/LEIE have all come back clear, plus the fingerprint check if they have lived out of state, invite the attendant into Empeon for the hiring paperwork: W-4, I-9, direct deposit and the attendant contract. Empeon invitations are manual, so this is a person doing it, not an automation. Then they may begin serving a consumer.

⚠️ FCSR Disqualifying Finding? If FCSR returns a disqualifying offense, the attendant CANNOT work under ANY circumstances until a Good Cause Waiver (GCW) is applied for AND approved by DHSS. Conditional employment is never permitted while awaiting GCW. If GCW is denied — the attendant cannot be hired. Reg: P&P Policy 13; CDS Program Req. §4.3
9
Execute Attendant Contract
Agency must have a contract with each personal care attendant. Even though the attendant is the consumer's employee, the vendor maintains the contract.
Reg: CDS Program Req. §4.4.1
10
Report New Hire to State of Missouri
Report new hire to Missouri Division of Employment Security (new hire reporting requirement). File under consumer's EIN.
11
Obtain FCSR Registration Number
Obtain attendant's FCSR number — required for EVV system. Record in attendant file.
11b
⚠️ Issue & Mail Permanent Agency ID Card to Attendant
This is a gap currently being implemented. At time of employment, mail a permanent ID card to the attendant. Card must display: (1) Agency name (Caring Companions), (2) Attendant's full name, (3) Title (Personal Care Attendant), (4) Attendant's signature. Attendant must carry this card at all times while working. Upon termination: request card be returned by mail. If unable to recover, document recovery attempts in writing and place in file.
Reg: P&P Policy 6 & 8; CDS Program Req. §5.6
STEP 4 — TRAINING & SETUP
12
Train Attendant on WellSky Personal Care (EVV)
Attendant must understand how to check in and out, either through the WellSky Personal Care app or by telephony from the consumer's home phone if that works better for them (portal: mycaringcds.com). EVV Correction Forms due by Saturday 11:59 PM each week. Train on fraud consequences of falsifying EVV. Attendant's FCSR# must be captured in EVV.
Reg: 13 CSR 70-3.320
13
Orient Attendant on Consumer's Care Plan
Attendant should understand the consumer's authorized tasks, hours, and limitations. Services must be delivered per the approved care plan only.
14
Orient Attendant on Fraud Prevention
Do not leave early without adjusting EVV. Do not claim hours not worked. Do not use EVV when consumer is hospitalized. False claims = fraud.
15
Payroll Setup Under Consumer's EIN (via Empeon)
Set up attendant in payroll system under the consumer's EIN (NOT Caring Companions' EIN 82-0968875). Pay rate: $15 to $16/hour. Direct deposit processes Thursdays (Wed before major holidays). Withhold and remit FICA, Medicare, federal and state income tax. Register attendant wages under consumer's UInteract account at uinteract.labor.mo.gov.
16
Establish LEIE Monthly Screening Schedule
Add attendant to monthly LEIE screening roster. Screen all aliases monthly. Document each screening.
Reg: CDS Program Req. §5.2 — Monthly requirement, non-negotiable
STEP 5 — ONGOING (POST-HIRE)
17
EDL Quarterly Re-Check
Re-screen all attendants against EDL every quarter. Document date and results.
Reg: RSMo 192.2490
18
FCSR Annual Re-Screen (Recommended)
DHSS recommends annual FCSR re-screening of all employed attendants. Document per PM-VM 17-31 guidance.

📌 EVV Correction Policy & Acceptable Reasons
✅ Acceptable Reasons for Manual Correction
  • Phone was dead / no battery at clock-in or out
  • App crashed or technical error (screenshot recommended)
  • No cell service at consumer's location (rural area)
  • Attendant forgot to clock in or out (occasional — not recurring)
  • WellSky app update caused disruption
  • Consumer's home phone not available for landline EVV
🚫 Red Flags — Patterns That Trigger MMAC Scrutiny
  • Same attendant requesting corrections repeatedly
  • Corrections that extend shift time (not just fix a missed clock)
  • Corrections submitted days after the visit (not same day)
  • No signed correction form on file for an adjustment
  • 3+ corrections in one month for the same attendant
  • 10+ corrections agency-wide in one month
  • Pattern of corrections always on the same day/consumer
⚠️ Documentation Rule: Every manual adjustment in WellSky must have a corresponding signed EVV Correction Form on file before the correction is made. If MMAC audits a claim and there is no form, the adjustment looks fraudulent. Saturday 11:59 PM weekly deadline still applies — corrections for the week must be in before that cutoff.

⚠️ Tax & Enrollment Setup
Forms Filed with IRS / MO:
Tax & Enrollment Setup
STEP 1 — Get Consumer's Federal EIN (IRS Form SS-4)
The consumer is their own employer and needs their own EIN — separate from Caring Companions' EIN.
1. Go to irs.gov → Tools → Apply for an EIN Online (free, instant).
2. Entity type: Individual / Sole Proprietor.
3. Reason: Hired employees.
4. Use the consumer's SSN, legal name, and home address.
5. Complete online, the EIN is issued immediately. On the final screen use the download button to save the CP 575 letter. Do not print the page: a printout of a web page is not an IRS-issued document and will not pass the Fusion audit. It is offered once and is never reissued, so if it is missed, ring 800-829-4933 and ask for a 147C.
6. Enter the EIN in the field below.
STEP 2 — IRS Form 8821 (Tax Information Authorization)
This authorizes Caring Companions to receive the consumer's IRS tax correspondence and speak to the IRS on their behalf.
⚠️ E-signed 8821s go online only. The IRS does not accept an electronically signed 8821 by fax or mail, and the Hub and GoHighLevel packets are e-signed.
1. Consumer signs Form 8821 in their enrollment packet.
2. Submit it at IRS.gov/Submit8821 (needs an IRS Secure Access account the first time).
3. Save the confirmation on the 8821 step. Only a paper 8821 signed by hand can be faxed or mailed.
STEP 3 — IRS Form 2678 (Employer/Payer Agent Appointment)
This designates Caring Companions as the agent authorized to handle FICA and FUTA payroll taxes on the consumer's behalf. IRS must approve — do not process payroll before approval.
⚠️ Wet/faxed signature required. IRS approval can take several weeks.
1. Complete Form 2678 with consumer's EIN and Caring Companions' EIN.
2. Consumer and Caring Companions both sign.
3. Mail to IRS. Wait for approval letter before first payroll run.
STEP 4A — MO Form 2643A (Missouri Tax Registration)
Registers the consumer with the Missouri Department of Revenue for state income tax withholding.
1. Complete Form 2643A using consumer's EIN, SSN, name, and home address.
2. Business type: Individual / Household employer.
3. Submit online (much faster than paper). Do not look for CDS inside our own MyTax account — it is not a tax type, and the employer being registered is the consumer, not us. Use the Online New Business Registration, signed out, once per consumer, and pick Withholding Tax.
4. You will receive the consumer's MO Withholding Tax ID — enter it in the MO Tax ID field below.
Phone: (573) 751-5860 | businesstaxregister@dor.mo.gov
STEP 4B — MO Form 2827 (Missouri Power of Attorney)
Authorizes Caring Companions to act on behalf of the consumer with the MO Department of Revenue for withholding tax matters.
1. Consumer signs Form 2827 with their MO Tax ID and EIN.
2. Submit to MO Dept of Revenue.
3. Keep a copy in the consumer's file.
STEP 5 — DES / UInteract (Missouri Unemployment Insurance Tax)
⚠️ TIMING: Cannot do this step until AFTER first payroll is issued AND consumer has paid $1,000+ in wages in a single quarter. DES will not issue an account number until then.

Before any of this: you need the CDS Vendor third-party login, created through "Reporting Service Signup" on UInteract. That signup is not where consumers get registered, it is what lets you register them. If you already log in and see your consumers, you have it.

If NEW consumer (never had a CDS vendor before):
Log in to UInteract with your CDS Vendor user ID, then Employer Registration → Register Employer. Enter your details as the person submitting, and Next. Everything after that is the consumer's details, screen by screen:

General Information
1. The CONSUMER's Federal Tax ID (EIN).
2. Type of Organization = Individual Ownership. Next.

Employer Entity Information
3. Consumer's first name, middle initial, last name. Leave Trade Name / DBA blank.
4. Paid employees for work performed in Missouri? Yes. Then the first worker date (when they first had an attendant) and the first payroll date (when they first paid one). If they have not paid wages you cannot finish the registration.
5. Agricultural work? No.
6. Employs housekeepers, sitters or other domestic employment? Yes.
7. Is this a general business? No.
8. Religious employer? No.  Federally recognised Indian tribe? No.
9. Paid unemployment insurance in another state (FUTA) this year or last? No.
10. Lessor / Professional Employment Organisation? No.  Leasing employees from another business? No.
11. Business locations in Missouri? Yes, then Continue.

Add Business Location / Headquarters
12. Number of Missouri employees at this location = the number of attendants.
13. Physical address = the CONSUMER's home address. County = where the consumer lives.
14. Describe the nature of your business: type CDS Consumer.
15. Principal Business Activity, three dropdowns in order: Health Care and Social Assistance → Social Assistance → Services for the Elderly and Persons with Disabilities.
16. Is this the primary business activity? Yes, Continue, then verify the address and Continue again.

Employer Contact Details
17. Unemployment Tax Mailing Address = the CONSUMER's home address.
18. Telephone = 000-000-0000. The consumer is never contacted. Fax blank.
19. Claims mailing address and payroll records address = Same as Unemployment Tax Mailing Address for both.
20. Contact Person for Unemployment Tax = your details. Continue.

Add Individual Ownership Details (the consumer)
21. Type of Individual Owner = Individual.
22. The consumer's SSN (required) and their name. Job Title = Owner.
23. Term begin and end dates: leave blank. Residential address = consumer's home address. Residential phone and email: leave blank.
24. Deceased? No, unless they are, in which case give the date of death. Continue, verify, Continue again.

The last few screens
25. Wage History: gross wages paid to the attendants for each quarter shown. Under $1,000 in every quarter means no account number.
26. Employment History: how many attendants worked in each week.
27. Business Acquisition: did you acquire this business? No.
28. Prior Registration: previously registered with Missouri? No.
29. Upload Documents and Tax and Wage Reports Received: neither applies, just Continue.
30. Statement of Acknowledgement: read it, I accept, Submit.
31. The confirmation screen shows the consumer's EAN and contribution rate. Record the EAN below. A letter follows in the post the next business day, and you can see it again by logging in later.

If you have to stop partway, click "Finish Later". Closing without it loses everything and the registration starts from the beginning.
If the EAN was not shown, or you closed the window before writing it down
First, the thing to rule out: if the consumer has never paid $1,000 in a single quarter, there is no EAN to find. DES does not issue one until then, so no amount of looking will turn one up. That is the usual reason it is missing.
Otherwise there are three ways to get it:
1. The list of all your consumers. Log in, then Inquiry → Tax Inquiry → Client List Details. Every consumer ever associated with us is there, with their EAN in the first column. This is the quickest way and it works even years later. Nobody is ever removed from that list.
2. The registration letter. View Correspondence, pick the consumer's account from the dropdown, Continue, then click the correspondence type to open it. The registration letter carries the EAN and the contribution rate. A paper copy is also posted the next business day.
3. Ring the CDS tax line on 573-751-1995 option 1, or email cdstax@labor.mo.gov.

Careful with two things on that Client List. "Association Status" always reads Active and is about our link to the consumer, not whether their account is open. And if the EAN ends in -01, -02 and so on, check the unit itself: Inquiry → Tax Inquiry → Employer Account, enter the first seven digits, Continue, then Details at the bottom right. A unit showing "Removed" is closed.

Worth doing once: Manage Alerts/Email Signup turns on an email whenever DES posts new correspondence, so a registration letter cannot sit unread. Be aware it stops the paper copies, so the email becomes the only notice you get.
If TRANSFERRED consumer (came from another CDS vendor):
If you are not sure whether they were with another vendor, try registering them in UInteract first. If you get an error, they are a transfer, and then:
1. Download MODES-5083 (Transferred Consumer Registration)
2. Fill in: your name and EIN, the consumer's EIN and SSN, the first date they paid wages since coming to us (never a future date), and the vendor they were with before. Check Fusion if you do not know who that was. Leave the account number blank if you do not have it.
3. Email (do NOT mail or fax) to cdstax@labor.mo.gov. A form missing any required item is rejected and sent back.
They may have no account at all if they never paid $1,000 in a quarter with the previous vendor.

After registration — quarterly wage reporting:
Login → Contribution and Wage Report → File Contribution and Wage Report. File oldest quarter first. Select Method A. Enter attendant SSN, name, and gross wages per quarter. Separate payment per consumer — never combine. If parent is the attendant: do NOT report those wages (not subject to UI tax).

Quarterly deadlines: Q1 (Jan–Mar): Apr 30 | Q2 (Apr–Jun): Jul 31 | Q3 (Jul–Sep): Oct 31 | Q4 (Oct–Dec): Jan 31
Late penalty: 10% of tax or $100/month, whichever is greater — max 20% or $200.

Questions: cdstax@labor.mo.gov | 573-751-1995 Opt. 1
Penalties/delinquent: Christopher Matzke — 573-751-1867
Wage reporting/adjustments: Kristie Riedmann — 573-751-1995 x4105
STEP 6 — Enter & upload in DHSS Fusion  ⚠️ THIS IS THE STEP THAT GETS AUDITED
Having the numbers is not enough. Per HCBS Manual 3.25 Appendix 1, two separate things are required, and a missing one is an audit finding referred to MMAC.

1. Type both numbers into Fusion. Participant page → “HCBS Eligibility” section → enter the Federal EIN and the Missouri Tax ID.

2. Upload proof. Participant’s electronic case record → “Documents” tab → category “EIN Tax Documents”.

Deadline for a new participant: proof uploaded within 90 days of the CDS start date. “New” means not yet authorized for CDS in their current case — someone authorized in a previous case still counts as new.

Accepted as proof of the FEDERAL EIN:
• CP 575 or 147C letter  • Form 940  • Form 941  • 8109 tax coupon
• An IRS letter showing the tax ID and legal name
• Any IRS document with the legal name and tax number preprinted

⛔ A W-9 is NOT accepted. Computer-printed forms are NOT accepted. This is the easiest way to fail the audit while believing you complied.
Accepted as proof of the MISSOURI EIN/TIN:
• A copy of the notice from the MO Department of Revenue  • MO 941  • MO W-3

Two ways you can be done early:
• One document showing both the federal and Missouri numbers covers both. No second upload.
• If a previous CDS vendor already uploaded verification to that case record, you do not need to upload again.

Remember whose numbers these are: the federal and state EINs belong to the consumer, not us, and they transfer with the consumer when they change agencies. That matters on every PCCP transfer.

Fusion access, logins or user accounts: HCBS.Systems@health.mo.gov (Bureau of Systems and Data Reporting).
⚠️ E-signed forms: an e-signed 8821 goes online only (IRS.gov/Submit8821). Form 2678 may still require an original signature — confirm with your accountant before marking filed.  |  ⚠️ DES: Cannot register in UInteract until after first payroll and $1,000+ paid in a single quarter.
START  ·  Enrollment packet
Signed in the Hub? Get the forms
Sent with the Send enrollment packet button on their lead. Each signed form is filled and saved on its own, ready to fax or mail.
Signed in GoHighLevel? Split the packet into separate forms
The consumer signs once and GoHighLevel gives back one 19-page PDF. Drop that PDF here and it comes apart into the eleven forms inside it, each one on its own and named, ready to fax or mail. Nothing leaves this browser: the splitting happens on your machine and only the finished forms are saved.
STEP 1  ·  Federal EIN (Form SS-4)  
The consumer is their own employer and needs their own EIN, separate from ours. Online is immediate; by fax about four business days and by mail about four weeks. Everything Missouri needs waits on this number.
Applying online? Use the download button on the final screen, not print. Printing the confirmation page gives you a picture of a web page, which is not an IRS-issued document and does not count as proof for Fusion. The download button gives the real CP 575 letter, it is offered once, and the IRS will not reissue it. If it was missed, ring 800-829-4933 (Mon-Fri, 7am-7pm local) and ask for a 147C letter, which they can fax while you wait. A 147C counts as proof exactly like a CP 575. Expect them to want the consumer on the call unless their 8821 is already on file.
STEP 2  ·  Form 8821  
Lets the IRS talk to us about this consumer. Without it on file they will want the consumer on the phone every time, including for a 147C.
STEP 3  ·  Form 2678  
Appoints us as the consumer's payroll agent for FICA and FUTA. Post only, and payroll cannot run until the IRS approves it, which takes weeks, so send this one early.
STEP 4  ·  Missouri registration (Form 2643A)  
You are registering the consumer as a household employer on their own EIN, not Caring Companions. One registration each, tax type Withholding Tax.
Start here, signed out: Online New Business Registration. Fill it in from their signed 2643A in the packet list. Needs the EIN first.
Allow 2-3 business days. The confirmation number above is the only thing you get at submission and is what Revenue will ask for. If nothing has arrived after a week, ring (573) 751-5860 with it and ask them to read you the account number.
STEP 4b  ·  Form 2827 (Missouri Power of Attorney)  
This is what lets us act for the consumer at the Department of Revenue. Nothing in the portal grants it; the signed form does.
STEP 5  ·  DES / UInteract (Missouri unemployment tax)  
New consumer: register in UInteract. Transferred consumer (came from another CDS vendor): download MODES-5083 — Transferred Consumer Registration — fill it in and email it to cdstax@labor.mo.gov. Do not mail or fax it. Questions: 573-751-1995 Opt. 1
STEP 6  ·  DHSS Fusion — this is the step that gets audited
⛔ A W-9 is not acceptable proof, nor is anything you typed yourself. Proof must come from the IRS or the MO Department of Revenue with the legal name and number already on it. Upload under the EIN Tax Documents category, or the auditor will not find it.
STEP 6b  ·  our own copy of the proof document
Keep the document here so the whole set is in one place if MMAC ever asks, and so a faxed 147C has somewhere to live before it goes into Fusion. This is our file copy, not the state's. The audited upload still has to be done in Fusion, then tick the box above.
LAST  ·  Empeon (payroll)
Do this last. Empeon needs the real EIN and MO Tax ID to exist first, so uploading before they do means doing it twice.

📞 What to say to somebody who has never heard of CDS

What the programme is. Medicaid can pay for someone to help you at home. There are two ways to do it. With an agency, the agency picks, hires, trains and supervises the caregiver. With Consumer Directed Services, you do: you choose the person, often somebody you already know and trust, and we handle the paperwork, the payroll and the state side.

Who it is for. To have Medicaid pay, the state has to find that your care needs are equal to nursing home care. You also have to be able to direct your own care, or have somebody legally able to direct it for you.

Do not promise them they qualify. The assessor scores them on a tool called the InterRAI HC, and 18 or higher is the line for Level of Care. Below that they are not eligible, whatever anybody hoped. It is kinder to say "the state decides, and here is what they look at" than to let somebody count on it.

Be honest about what it is not. It is not 24-hour care and it is not total care. It is extra help on top of what you already have, and it only covers what you need now, not what you might need later.

What happens next. A referral goes to the state. An HCBS assessor rings to arrange a visit to your home, face to face, and works out what you qualify for. You can have anyone you like with you for that visit.

Say this plainly, it is the bit that goes wrong. The assessor will try you once. If you miss it they leave a message or send a letter and you have 10 days to ring back. Miss that and the referral closes and you start again. So answer unknown numbers for the next couple of weeks.

Tell them to have ready: their MO HealthNet (Medicaid) number, date of birth and Social Security number, because the assessor has to verify who they are speaking to. Guardianship or power of attorney paperwork if there is any.

And ask them to name us. The assessor asks which provider they want. Give the full business name and our number: Caring Companions Consumer Directed Services, (417) 218-2888.

The HCBS-1 says ALL FIELDS REQUIRED. These are its own questions in its own order, so filling this in on the call means the form can go straight out afterwards without ringing anybody back. Form MO 580-3377, returned to HCBSCallCenterReferrals@health.mo.gov.
Person being referred
Where they live
Responsible party or guardian
Communication
In hospital or a facility right now?
Living arrangements
Why they need help
The rest of the form
Where they are with the state
Three ways in: the online HCBS Referral form, by phone on 1-866-835-3505, or the paper HCBS-1 emailed to HCBSCallCenterReferrals@health.mo.gov. Afterwards, check where it has got to under the Referral and PCCP Request tabs in Fusion. The assessor rings once and the referral closes after 10 days of silence, so that warning is worth more to a caller than anything else on this call.
